rationale: Use own colour and the column's nonzero colour set. Columns containing exactly {1,2} recolour 1 and 2 to 8; {2,3} recolours 3 to 9; {1} recolours zeros to 3. Demonstration 2 exhibits all three changes.
Column sets determine the changes: {1,2,3} maps 0 to 8 and 2 to 7; {1,3} maps 0 to 5; {2,3} maps 2 to 0. Demonstration 1 shows the first two cases, and demonstration 2 shows the third.
Use column colour sets: {1,2,3} maps 0 to 2 and 1 to 0; {1,2} maps 2 to 9; {1,3} maps 0 to 2. In demonstration 1, column 3 exhibits the first rule and column 1 maps its 2 to 9.

Use full 3x3 neighbourhoods including boundary padding. Demonstration 8 changes the top-left zero to 7 with a 2 immediately below; demonstration 10 changes the top-left zero to 6 with an all-zero in-grid 2x2 neighbourhood. Other demonstrated neighbourhoods preserve their centre colours.

Use full 3x3 neighbourhoods. Demonstration 2 changes the top-right zero to 4, while demonstration 5 changes row 3, column 6 to 5. Boundary padding and surrounding colours distinguish these keys from unchanged zeros.

Column sets {1,3} map 0 to 4; {1,2,3} map 0 and 3 to 6; {3} maps 0 to 9. Demonstration 1 shows the first two rules, and demonstration 3 shows zeros becoming 9 in columns containing only nonzero colour 3.

Use nearest nonzero colours in each cardinal direction. Demonstration 1 maps a zero with no colour above, 1 below, and 3 on both sides to 1. Demonstrations 2 and 5 map zeros with no colour above or left, 3 below, and 1 right to 5.

Use full 3x3 neighbourhoods. Demonstration 10 changes row 5, column 6 from 0 to 2: its neighbourhood has a right boundary and zeros at every in-grid position. The other demonstrations preserve their shown neighbourhood centres.
Every demonstration maps border colours 0 to 5, 1 to 6, 2 to 1, and 3 to 9 while preserving interior colours. Demonstration 1 shows all four border mappings and unchanged interior 0, 1, 2, and 3.

Use own colour together with both row and column nonzero sets. Demonstration 1 maps a zero with row set {1,2} and column set {2,3} to 4; demonstration 3 maps a 2 with row set {1,2,3} and column set {2,3} to 4; demonstration 6 maps a 2 with both sets {1,2,3} to 3.
